title: The Mass Gap of SU(N) Gauge Theory Seen by an Observer of Fixed Physical Resolution
description:
We take the frame of the Entroptics paper, an observer as a finite aperture whose mode count is read from the signal's spectrum, as the method for the continuum limit of four-dimensional SU(N) Wilson lattice gauge theory, and use it in two places. On the gap side the theory is read at a window it sets: the doubling defect D_β(w) = 16 log Z_β(2^w) − log Z_β(2^(w+1)) of the periodic torus, a finite-size free energy with the bulk cancelled exactly (read, as an argued interpretation, as a weighted sum of Rényi-2 entropies of transfer operators), is held at a fixed value u_0 along a coupling tower while the window doubles. On the existence side the observer's screen in a box of fixed physical side is a finite family of modes, and one variance bound with per-mode hypercontractivity gives every even moment through the Rényi count of order 1/2, with constants free of the box and the zoom; for the single-reading closure, 1/2 is the sharp order; for the Wilson field itself the count bound is reduced to one fine-scale inequality, which is open.

For N ≥ 2 we prove that the formalized target CS(N), an Osterwalder–Schrader form of the existence-and-gap statement (separated test functions, a limit along a fixed ultrafilter, no Wightman reconstruction), follows from three open statements: (S), that the defect tends to 0 along the windows at arbitrarily large β; (M), that at window couplings arbitrarily close to 0, along every coupling tower, the measured tensor mass stays in a band of ratio 2 at a level chosen per tower; and (E), the existence clauses restated along towers. A fixed-level form of (M) is refuted under (S). Without hypotheses we prove the doubling bootstrap, in which one window with D ≤ 1/1000 forces D(w+1) ≤ 250 D(w)² and a transfer gap uniform in the torus size (a four-dimensional form of the purity bootstrap of OpenAI's O(3) work, of OpenAI's proof of the Haldane gap and of Grover's extensions of it); vanishing on an interval of small β, at the decoupled end of the anisotropic family and on an explicit strip of mixed couplings that shrinks with β; box gaps for SU(2) and SU(3) at small coupling; and a list of properties that do not separate SU(N) from U(1). Against the OpenAI construction of pure Yang–Mills theory we prove that its Wilson laws, with its SU(N) and its Haar measure, are those used here at twice the coupling, and that its trace law gives a kernel satisfying the asymptotic-freedom clause of the target; and we prove that a seed at a side of bounded physical size along its couplings, which is open, gives its SU(N) lattice family a transfer gap and clustering uniform in the spacing and the volume, with the abstract steps from clustering to equal components and to a Hamiltonian gap. That its reconstruction meets the hypotheses of those steps is the open link of that route. The theorems are formalized in Lean 4. The mass gap is not proved.

The Lean 4 / Mathlib development depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Monte Carlo data are validation only.

The record holds the paper (research/paper/mass-gap.pdf and its sources), the Lean development, the exact checks and the analysis code. Code: Apache-2.0. Paper text: CC BY 4.0. The lattice ensembles are a separate dataset record, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22850110.
